subject: Order form insurance: split-limits / additional insured process
messages:
From: Nate Reynolds <nate@cloudcorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: COI / endorsement ask for order form

Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Quick question on the Order Form insurance language — our procurement team needs to know whether Redwood can accept a split-limits presentation for Auto/GL (e.g., $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate) on the COI, and whether an Additional Insured can be listed on the COI itself or whether you require an endorsement naming CloudCorp on the carrier letterhead.

Attached is our standard COI request form for reference (CloudCorp_COI_Request_Form.pdf).

If endorsement is required, our broker indicates it could take up to 10 business days after signature. Can you confirm:
- Is a COI with Additional Insured sufficient for order activation?
- If not, is a 30-day window to deliver endorsement acceptable?

We have a planned go-live for 12/01, so any timing constraints matter.

Thanks,
Nate
Nate Reynolds
Vendor Contracts / CloudCorp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nate Reynolds <nate@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: COI / endorsement ask for order form

Nate — thanks for the clear ask and the COI form. Forwarding a short summary so you can route to procurement/broker as needed.

Summary / proposed stance from Redwood:
- Split limits: Acceptable if the aggregate meets our minimums in the Order Form (we require at least $2M GL aggregate or equivalent; $1M/$2M split as you described meets this).
- Additional Insured: We prefer the endorsement on carrier letterhead (CG 20 10 or equivalent) because it provides contractual standing; however for order activation we can accept a COI that names CloudCorp as Additional Insured as an interim measure provided that an endorsement is delivered within 30 days of effective date.

I attached a redline snippet for the Order Form and MSA clause that reflects the interim-COI + 30-day-endorsement approach (proposed_redline_msa.docx). The key language to add would be: "Seller may provide a COI naming Customer as Additional Insured for order activation; Seller must procure and deliver the required endorsement on carrier letterhead within 30 calendar days of the Effective Date. Failure to deliver endorsement constitutes a material breach and entitles Customer to suspend services until cure."

If your broker needs to confirm the endorsement window, please have them loop in Kimberly (copied) — she handles carrier escalation and can advise on standard carrier timing.

Happy to hop on a brief call if helpful.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Leila Gomez <legal@cloudcorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nate Reynolds <nate@cloudcorp.com>, CloudCorp Broker <broker@insureco.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: COI / endorsement ask for order form

Jonas — thanks. Quick note from our broker (attached carrier_response.pdf): some carriers will issue a COI naming an Additional Insured immediately but will not issue a formal endorsement until after policy changes are processed and signature is complete. Broker confirms they can deliver a COI that lists CloudCorp as Additional Insured at binding, and an endorsement within 10-15 business days in most cases, but for certain carriers the endorsement issuance could slide to ~25 business days.

CloudCorp preference is to have the endorsement on file within 30 days; procurement is willing to accept a COI for immediate activation provided there is a firm commitment from the broker and a documented outage/penalty plan if the endorsement is delayed.

Attaching the broker note for transparency.

Regards,
Leila Gomez
Sr. Counsel, CloudCorp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leila Gomez <legal@cloudcorp.com>, Nate Reynolds <nate@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T16:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: COI / endorsement ask for order form

Appreciate the quick turn here, Leila. Kimberly — can you confirm from a carrier/operations perspective that the 30-calendar-day endorsement window is workable and that we can commit to the interim-COI for activation? If certain carriers push beyond 30 business days (as the broker noted), we should capture that exception explicitly and propose either a temporary credit or the right for CloudCorp to suspend until the endorsement is provided.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to confirm standard carrier timing and flag any carriers for which 30 calendar days is not achievable.
2) If any carrier exceptions exist, we draft an exception clause and share for CloudCorp legal review (Laura, can you own the exception text?).
3) Schedule a 30-minute alignment call this week with Nate, Leila, Kimberly, and Laura to finalize acceptance criteria and delivery commitments.

I can be the single thread owner to drive sign-off.

Thanks — looking to lock this before your planned go-live on 12/01.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
